description: Limit vectors for wire-v0 section 6: each limit just at and just past its bound, under the default limits unless a vector carries `limits` (merged over the defaults). Hex is body bytes only. `plan` selects row@1 or columnar@5. Values of the form {"$bytes": "<hex>"} denote a bytes value. `valid` vectors round-trip; `invalidDecode` and `invalidEncode` fail with `error`; `decodeOnly` vectors decode to `value`, while an encoder holding the same limits refuses that value with `limit` (each also appears in `invalidEncode`). Decoders and encoders both run them.

valid.name: amplification-at-bound
valid.description: 32 zero-payload rows with no bytes after the count: exactly maxAmplification x (0 + 1)

valid.name: col-amplification-at-bound
valid.description: 128 rows of a width-zero column: 3 bytes follow the count, 32 x (3 + 1) = 128

valid.name: budget-nested-at-bound
valid.description: 64 inner arrays of 32 rows each pass their own bound; the counts sum to 64 + 64 x 32 = 2112 = 32 x (65 + 1)

valid.name: budget-fixed-at-bound
valid.description: fixed lengths are charged too: 2 + 2 x 15 = 32 items in an empty body

valid.name: max-items-fixed-at-bound
valid.description: maxItems applies to a declared length too

valid.name: max-depth-at-bound
valid.description: the int is enclosed by nullable, struct, nullable: depth 3

valid.name: fixed-amplification-at-bound
valid.description: b (01 ff) comes first, so 0 bytes remain on entering a: 32 <= 32 x (0 + 1); budget 32 x (2 + 1) = 96

valid.name: col-budget-at-bound
valid.description: 128 rows within the amplification bound (32 x (3 + 1)) and maxTotalItems 128

valid.name: col-charged-once-at-bound
valid.description: 04 rows, 05 presence (rows 0 and 2), 00 raw, 02 06 = 1, 3: n = 4 rows, k = 2 participate; charged once with n, 4 <= maxTotalItems 4 (n + k = 6 would not be)

invalidDecode.name: budget-nested-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: 65 inner arrays of 32 rows: every count passes its own bound, but the sum 65 + 65 x 32 = 2145 exceeds 32 x (66 + 1) = 2144

invalidDecode.name: budget-fixed-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: 2 + 2 x 16 = 34 items in an empty body; each fixed length alone is within 32

invalidDecode.name: max-items-fixed-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: a declared length of 5 is rejected on entry under maxItems 4, though all 5 elements are present

invalidDecode.name: max-depth-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: the int is enclosed by nullable, struct, nullable, struct: depth 4

invalidDecode.name: max-depth-before-count
invalidDecode.description: the array sits at depth 4: depth is checked on entering it, before its count 5 is read against maxItems 4

invalidDecode.name: fixed-amplification-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: 33 > 32 x (0 + 1) on entering a, though the body holds 2 bytes and the budget is 96

invalidDecode.name: budget-siblings-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: 6 + 6 = 12 items exceed maxTotalItems 10; each array alone is within every per-array bound

invalidDecode.name: col-budget-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: the same 128 rows pass the amplification bound but exceed maxTotalItems 127

invalidDecode.name: col-charged-once-over-bound
invalidDecode.description: the same body under maxTotalItems 3: the charge is n = 4, not k = 2

invalidEncode.name: encode-amplification-later-sibling
invalidEncode.description: the decodeOnly vector of the same name: refused by the encoder

decodeOnly.name: amplification-later-sibling
decodeOnly.description: 11 bytes (b) remain at a's count, so a decoder allows 32 x (11 + 1) = 384 rows; the encoder measures only a's own 0 bytes after its count and refuses 33 > 32
